welcome: Hi! I'm an AI bot that writes code. Your job is to guide me using unit tests.
slogan: ![Logo of UnitTestGame](../apple-touch-icon.png)Learn to write unit tests that guide an AI bot.
invitation: Which level do you want to play?
closeTab: Well done! You've completed all the levels. You can now write unit tests for your own projects.
addUnitTestButton: I want to add this unit test
submitUnitTestsButton: I want to submit the unit tests
unitTestNotAdded: I didn't add the unit test, because it doesn't match the *Specification*.
tooManyUnitTests: You've tested the *Current Function* thoroughly, but you wrote {numberOfUnnecessaryUnitTests} more {numberOfUnnecessaryUnitTests === 1 ? 'unit test' : 'unit tests'} than necessary. {numberOfRedundantUnitTests === 1 ? 'The following' : 'At least one of the following'} can be left out.
readSpecification: First, read the *Specification*. Then write a unit test that the *Current Function* fails.
improveCurrentFunction: After adding a unit test I'll improve the *Current Function* so all *Unit Tests* pass again.
submitUnitTests: Submit the *Unit Tests* when you think the *Current Function* matches the *Specification*.
currentFunctionNotImproved: I've added the unit test, but the *Current Function* already passes it, so I didn't improve the *Current Function*.
hint: Write a unit test that the *Current Function* fails.
currentFunctionImproved: I've added the unit test to the *Unit Tests* and improved the *Current Function* so the new unit test now passes{numberOfUnitTests === 1 ? '' : ' as well'}.
invalidUnitTest: The following unit test doesn't match the *Specification*, but the *Current Function* passes it.
moreUnitTests: The *Current Function* doesn't match the *Specification* yet. You need at least {numberOfUnitTestsStillNeeded} more {numberOfUnitTestsStillNeeded === 1 ? 'unit test' : 'unit tests'}, so write a unit test that matches the *Specification* and that the *Current Function* fails.
currentFunctionCorrect: Well done! The *Current Function* matches the *Specification*.
wrongAction: Hmm, that's not quite right. Try again.
addBatteryLevel20: The *Specification* contains the number `20`. That is a good starting point. When the battery level is `20`, the function must return `"NORMAL MODE"`.
addBatteryLevel19: The *Current Function* now always returns `"NORMAL MODE"`, but the *Specification* says battery level `19` must return `"LOW POWER MODE"`. Add a unit test for that.
submitUnitTestsFirst: The *Current Function* can now return either `"NORMAL MODE"` or `"LOW POWER MODE"`. Submit the *Unit Tests* to check if the *Current Function* matches the *Specification*.
addBatteryLevel21: The *Current Function* now returns `"NORMAL MODE"` only for battery level `20`. The *Specification* says `21` must also return `"NORMAL MODE"`. Add a unit test for that.
submitUnitTestsSecond: Submit the *Unit Tests* again to check if the *Current Function* matches the *Specification*.
addBatteryLevel18: The *Current Function* now returns `"LOW POWER MODE"` only for battery level `19`. The *Specification* says `18` must also return `"LOW POWER MODE"`. Add a unit test for that.
submitUnitTestsThird: Submit the *Unit Tests* again to check if the *Current Function* finally matches the *Specification*.
batteryLevelSpecification: A smartphone normally operates in `"NORMAL MODE"`, but when the battery level is less than `20`, it operates in `"LOW POWER MODE"`.
votingAgeSpecification: You can vote if your age is `18` or over.
windScaleSpecification: It's `"CALM"` if the wind speed is less than `20`, `"BREEZE"` if less than `50`, `"GALE"` if less than `90`, and `"STORM"` otherwise.
reviewSpecification: Your review is `"GOOD"` if the price is less than `20` and the quality is at least `7`, `"BAD"` if the price is `20` or more and the quality is less than `7`, and `"OK"` otherwise.
discountSpecification: You get `20`% discount if the total is at least `200` and you have a member card, `10`% if the total is at least `100` or you have a member card, and `0`% otherwise.
fizzBuzzSpecification: Say `"FIZZ"` if the number is divisible by 3, `"BUZZ"` if divisible by 5, `"FIZZBUZZ"` if divisible by both 3 and 5, and `"NUMBER"` for any other number.
leapYearSpecification: Return `true` if the year is a leap year and `false` otherwise. A year is a leap year if it is divisible by 4. The exception is that years divisible by 100 are not leap years, unless they are also divisible by 400.
triangleTypeSpecification: The type of the triangle is `"EQUILATERAL"`, `"ISOSCELES"`, or `"SCALENE"`. A triangle is `"EQUILATERAL"` if all three sides have the same length. A triangle is `"ISOSCELES"` if exactly two sides have the same length. A triangle is `"SCALENE"` if all three sides have different lengths.
speedDisplaySpecification:
The speed sensor reports the speed in tenths of kilometers per hour (e.g. 131 means 13.1 km/h). Show the speed on the display as `"DECIMAL"` if a decimal fits (e.g. 131 → `"DECIMAL"` because 13.1 fits on the display), or `"INTEGER"` otherwise (e.g. 826 → `"INTEGER"` because 82.6 doesn't fit on the display but 83 does). If the car isn't moving, it's `"START"`. If the speed no longer fits on the display, it's `"DANGER"` (e.g. 3000 → `"DANGER"`).
The display looks like this, where every X is a LED light:
+-------------------+
|  X   XXXX   XXXX  |
|  X   X  X   X  X  |
|  X   XXXX   XXXX  |
|  X   X  X   X  X  |
|  X   XXXX X XXXX  |
|                   |
| X START  DANGER X |
+-------------------+
parkingFeeSpecification: The parking fee is `0` cents if the car is parked for less than a half hour, or if the customer has shopped on the weekend. It's `1000` cents if it's a weekend. Otherwise, it's 5 cents per minute if the customer hasn't shopped, or 3 cents per minute if the customer has shopped.
